newsitem.title: USA: Tele-Comms spending more on marketing.
newsitem.headline: Tele-Comms spending more on marketing.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc is spending about $100 million on marketing in the second half of the year, President and Chief Operating Officer Leo Hindery said.
The company spent $25 million on marketing in the second quarter and only $14 million in the first quarter, which Hindery called "pitiful."
"If I don't get subs (subscribers) in the fourth quarter I'm going to kill myself," Hindery told reporters on a teleconference call.
"We know how to market cable around here. We just didn't do it," he said, referring to the lower marketing budget earlier in the year.
TCI will spend $53 million on marketing in the third quarter and $50 million in the final quarter.
Hindery cautioned the extra spending will not help much in the third quarter because of the typical summer lull.

He attributed the loss of 89,000 cable customers in the second quarter to seasonal factors, such as college students going home and disconnecting their cable service, and to customer dissatisfaction over rate increases.

Hindery said he assumed that customers who were lost to a competitor were going to direct broadcast satellite (DBS) because "I always believe the worst." He vowed not to lose any more customers to DBS.

Hindery also said that by the end of the year some 90 percent of the homes TCI serves will be "technically ready for digital." However, digital marketing will only go to about two-thirds of those customers because some will be transfered to joint ventures and "it's not appropriate to launch digital if the ownership changes."

He said in all more than four million customers will have been transferred to joint ventures, some of which will not close till late in the fourth quarter or early in the first. Some partnerships have already been announced. TCI ended the quarter with about 14,198,000 customers.
